content.title: About
content.content: Egg quesadilla is a Mexican dish consisting of a thin corn or wheat tortilla filled with scrambled egg and often complemented by cheese, vegetables, and spices. It cooks quickly, is nutritious, and works well for breakfast or a light dinner.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The word “quesadilla” comes from the Spanish “queso,” meaning cheese, although the original version may omit cheese.
Adding egg makes the dish more filling and provides a high‑quality protein source, popular among athletes.
Tortillas used can be corn or wheat, influencing flavor and texture.
In Mexico, quesadillas are commonly served with salsa, guacamole, and sour cream.
Fast preparation time (about 5‑7 minutes) makes it a favorite for busy people.

items.title: Rich source of protein
items.content: Eggs provide high‑quality protein essential for muscle growth and tissue repair.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Eggs contain B2, B6, and B12 vitamins that support energy metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Healthy fats
items.content: When cheese is added, the dish includes monounsaturated and polyunsaturated fats beneficial for heart health.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: Eggs and tortillas supply iron, zinc, and phosphorus, important for bones and immunity.

items.title: Low in carbs
items.content: Egg quesadilla fits moderate low‑carb diets, especially when using whole‑grain tortillas.

items.title: Egg allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to eggs, ranging from skin rashes to anaphylaxis.

items.title: Cholesterol content
items.content: Eggs contain cholesterol; people with high cholesterol should monitor their intake.

items.title: Salt and fat in add‑ons
items.content: Cheese and sauces can increase sodium and saturated fat levels, which should be considered in a balanced diet.

items.title: Tortilla quality
items.content: Refined‑flour tortillas have a higher glycemic index; whole‑grain options are preferable.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Heat a skillet and lightly oil it. Place a tortilla, spread beaten egg over it, add shredded cheese and any vegetables (tomatoes, spinach, bell pepper). Fold the tortilla in half and cook until golden and the cheese melts, about 2‑3 minutes per side.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Best enjoyed fresh. Store leftovers in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2 days. Reheat in a skillet or oven to retain a crisp crust.
